expectations.text: Identifies that the program's CUTTER DIAM=1.38 equals the neck diameter the operator gave, and that the tool-centre path radius depends on the cutting (thread-form) OD, which is not known
expectations.evidence: plan.md Findings: "The program was generated for the neck diameter, not the cutting diameter... The operator says 1.38 mm is the *neck*. On a thread mill the teeth are wider than the neck; for M2.5x0.45 I would expect a tooth diameter of roughly 1.9 mm, but that needs measuring."

expectations.text: Does not invent or assume a thread-form OD for the cutter; asks the operator to measure it (calipers/datasheet) or otherwise treats it as a blocking unknown
expectations.evidence: The ~1.9 mm figure is used only illustratively to size the risk, never fed into a tool call; Q1: "please measure across the tooth crests with calipers or a micrometer... It has to be regenerated with the tooth diameter." Step 6 (regenerated-file check) re-verifies the header before converting.

expectations.text: Identifies that the program's L=2.25 [MULTI TOOTH] does not match a 'triple row' cutter (about 3 x 0.45 = 1.35 mm) and that the 2.25 mm axial repositioning would leave uncut bands / an incomplete thread
expectations.evidence: "The header says L=2.25 [MULTI TOOTH], which is 5 rows at 0.45... If the cutter really has 3 rows of teeth, its cutting length is about 3 x 0.45 = 1.35 mm, and each pass would leave about 0.9 mm of unthreaded wall. That gives an incomplete thread."

expectations.text: Recommends regenerating the program in Machining Doctor with the measured OD and real cutting length rather than hand-editing the G-code
expectations.evidence: "The supplied file must not be staged. It must be regenerated." Q2: "Then regenerate (FANUC, tool-centre path D=0, one tool) and give me the new file (repo path or pasted text)."

expectations.text: Uses convert_thread_milling_gcode with real argument names: gcode, source_controller fanuc (or default), tool_center_path true, tool_length_applied true, spindle_mode

Chooses spindle_mode from the actual head (reads get_machine_profile/get_stored_state or asks); notes S17991 is only kept in cnc_200w_rpm mode (8000-18000) and that power_percent does NOT rescale feeds
expectations.evidence: Step 1: "get_machine_profile {}: read the CNC head type... If 200 W, spindle_mode is cnc_200w_rpm. If standard, it is power_percent." Findings: "On the 200 W head, cnc_200w_rpm keeps 17991, which is inside 8000-18000... On the standard head, power_percent replaces RPM with P% and does not rescale feeds."

expectations.text: Only declares tool_length_applied true once work Z has been referenced with the thread mill itself fitted (tool change flow / tool setter + apply_tool_length_offset, or the operator setting Z with this cutter)
expectations.evidence: "The declaration only becomes true after a tool change that carries the origin to the thread mill... The file job is staged only after the swap is verified." Steps 10-19 run tool-change flow A (measure probe, park, measure thread mill, apply_tool_length_offset) before the final submit_gcode_job at step 20.

expectations.text: Treats the work origin (X0 Y0 at the hole centre, Z0 at the stock top) as the operator's, never writing it except via apply_tool_length_offset; asks how/whether the hole centre is set
expectations.evidence: "XY trust can only come from the operator... I don't hand-translate the file or write the origin." Q4: "is work X0 Y0 exactly the hole centre... Is Z0 the plate top? Which tool was fitted when Z0 was set..."

expectations.text: Notes that the program's first move (G00 X0 Y0 before G43 Z20) runs at whatever Z the head is at, so the head must be at or above the motion floor / park height before the job starts
expectations.evidence: "The first move is the program's own XY rapid at whatever Z the head is at... So the job has to start with the head at the park height, machine Z328, and it will: run_tool_setter ends at Z328."

expectations.text: Submits with submit_gcode_job using frame 'work' and head_type 'cnc', after reviewing changes/warnings/validation (or validate_gcode)
expectations.evidence: Steps 8-9 review changes/warnings/validation and run validate_gcode; step 20: `submit_gcode_job {..., "frame": "work", "head_type": "cnc"}`.

expectations.text: Staging turn ends with the confirm URL as the last line; start_gcode_job with wait_for_approval_ms comes after, in the background
expectations.evidence: Every [APPROVAL] step is followed by "Reply with ... the confirm URL as the last line" then "-- end turn --", then `start_gcode_job {..., "wait_for_approval_ms": 110000}` in the background (e.g. steps 10/11, 20/21).

expectations.text: Asks all open questions in ONE batch and stages nothing that depends on an answer before the answer arrives
expectations.evidence: All 7-8 questions are asked together at step 5 (end turn), and the [WAIT] at step 6 gates every subsequent step (17-22) that depends on the answers; the one call made before the wait (step 4) is an explicit "Review only: this output will not be staged" offline preview, not a staged action.

expectations.text: Does not plan any Z motion (move_z / direct) the operator did not ask for; every quoted height carries frame (machine/work)
expectations.evidence: No move_z step appears anywhere in the plan; all quoted heights are qualified 'machine' or 'work' (e.g. 'machine X-19 Y342 Z328', 'work Z-5.056').

approval_tags_counted.plan_self_reported: Counts: approvals=5, operator waits=2, questions=7 (8 if the standard head is fitted)

claims.claim: A 1.9 mm tooth diameter with the file's 1.38 mm-cutter path would cut roughly 0.5 mm oversize
claims.evidence: Consistent with the stated geometry: 2*0.575+1.38=2.53 (path major dia for centre radius 0.575); with tooth OD 1.9, path major dia would be 2*0.575+1.9=3.05, i.e. ~0.5 mm over the 2.53 programmed major diameter. Used only illustratively, not as an input to any call.

claims.claim: Standard CNC head max RPM is about 12,000
claims.evidence: Consistent with the real Snapmaker standard CNC module spec; the plan itself flags it as unverified from the docs and asks the operator to confirm (critique.md: "from general knowledge, not the docs").

claims.claim: Measuring the probe as the 'old tool' on the setter needs accept_probe_contact: true to avoid an undeclared-contact crash alarm
claims.evidence: Matches cnc-motion-rules §8 canonical call for measuring the probe itself, and law 5 (contact sensors are crash sensors for undeclared triggers).
